title: Procurement ↔ Billing Traceability Playbook — Contract Milestones to Forecast Adjustments
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook documents the end-to-end handoff and mapping between signed procurement/contract events and the systems that drive billing and revenue forecast adjustments. It is intended for Finance (RevenueOps), Procurement, Legal, Sales Operations, and Customer Success teams. The objective is to ensure deterministic, auditable triggers for invoicing, revenue recognition input, and forecast updates so we minimize billing lag, incorrect forecasts, and downstream disputes.

Scope:
- Applies to all customer engagements that create recurring or milestone-based revenue (Hosted Redwood API, Redwood Dedicated reservations, Redwood Private deployments, professional services and on-prem packaging fees).
- Covers contract signature -> PO issuance -> revenueops intake -> billing trigger -> forecast adjustment loop.
- Excludes one-off refunds and credit memos (see Billing SOP: refunds).

Definitions:
- Contract Effective Date: the date on which both parties have executed the contract.
- Billing Trigger: event or metadata condition that causes an invoice to be generated (e.g., start-of-service, milestone reached, 30-day net payment after invoice).
- Forecast Event: signal consumed by FP&A that changes forward revenue projection (e.g., signed contract, amendment, cancellation).
- PO: Purchase Order from customer that references our order form or SOW.
- RevOps System: system of record for revenue contracts (Salesforce + RevOps connector to ERP/billing).

Principles and SLOs:
- Traceability: every invoice line must be traceable to a contract clause or approved PO.
- Timeliness: billing trigger must be created in RevOps within 3 business days of Contract Effective Date for Hosted API and Dedicated; 5 business days for Private/on‑prem packages requiring security review.
- Forecast alignment: FP&A forecast must be updated within 2 business days of RevOps marking a contract as 'Committed'.
- Escalation latency: disputes or missing PO issues >7 business days must be escalated to Finance leadership.

Roles & Ownership:
- Procurement: verifies PO compliance, validates supplier-side procurement terms where Redwood purchases services/hardware; notifies RevOps when customer PO is received.
- Legal: approves contract language and confirms contract effective date; flags nonstandard revenue clauses (e.g., milestone-based recognition).
- Sales / Account Team: confirms SOW deliverables, start dates, and any implementation milestones; routes signed contract + SOW to RevOps and Procurement.
- RevOps (RevenueOps / Billing): creates billing triggers in the billing system, tags contracts with revenue model (recurring, milestone, one-time), and notifies FP&A.
- FP&A: ingests RevOps signals to update rolling forecasts and informs Treasury for cashflow planning.

Procedure: Contract to Invoice (high-level)
1) Contract executed: Sales uploads executed contract and SOW to the contract repository (Salesforce Contract record + link to document storage).
2) Legal confirmation: Legal updates the contract record with "effective_date", revenue model note, and any special recognition language within 24 hours of receipt.
3) Procurement validation (if PO required by customer): Procurement confirms PO number matches contract value and scope; assigns PO status = VALID or PENDING_CLARIFICATION and uploads PO to the contract record.
4) RevOps intake: RevOps validates metadata (start date, billing cadence, currency, invoice recipient) and creates the Billing Trigger in the RevOps system. Billing Trigger must include: contract_id, po_number (optional), start_date, billing_cadence, rev_model, customer_billing_contact, invoice_terms.
5) Billing execution: Billing system generates the first invoice per the trigger. For recurring Hosted API contracts we use monthly upfront invoices by default unless otherwise specified.
6) Forecast update: RevOps emits a Commit signal and FP&A updates the forecast within 2 business days.
7) Close the loop: RevOps and Procurement confirm PO issuance and invoice sent; Customer Success confirms implementation milestones (if milestone-based billing) and updates RevOps when milestones complete.

Detailed workflow table (key fields and owners):
| Step | System | Primary Owner | Required Fields | SLA |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| Contract Upload | Salesforce / DocStore | Sales | contract_id, effective_date, sdl_user, sig_pages | 1 business day |
| Legal Review | DocStore / Legal queue | Legal | legal_notes, rev_rec_flags | 1 business day |
| PO Validation | Procurement system | Procurement | po_number, po_amount, po_date | 2 business days |
| Billing Trigger Create | RevOps system | RevOps | contract_id, start_date, cadence, currency, invoice_terms | 3 business days |
| Invoice Issued | Billing/ERP | Billing | invoice_id, invoice_date, amount, line_items | Per billing cadence |
| Forecast Commit | FP&A tools | FP&A | commit_amount, ARR_delta, notes | 2 business days |

Approval & Thresholds (Procurement):
- Purchases and contractual commitments requested by Redwood teams follow this approval matrix when Redwood is the purchaser:
  - < $25K: Line manager approval.
  - $25K–$100K: Procurement + Finance partner approval.
  - $100K–$250K: Procurement + Finance + Legal review.
  - > $250K: CPO/CFO approval and Procurement Director sign-off.
- Customer-side PO requirements: if the customer requires a PO to accept services, Procurement must mark PO received before RevOps creates the Billing Trigger unless Sales documents an exception approved by RevenueOps.

RACI Example (milestone-based engagement):
| Activity | Sales | Legal | Procurement | RevOps | Customer Success | FP&A |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Negotiate contract | R | C | A | I | C | I |
| Approve contract | R | A | I | I | C | I |
| Receive PO | I | I | R | C | I | I |
| Create billing trigger | I | I | C | R | I | I |
| Record forecast commit | I | I | I | C | I | R |

Billing Trigger examples and edge cases:
- Recurring (Hosted API): create monthly invoice with usage settlement; billing trigger includes usage bucket and overage terms.
- Dedicated reserved capacity: create invoice for reservation fee at contract start (prepaid monthly/quarterly as agreed); include contract-specific SLA credits as separate credit-memo line items.
- Private/on-prem: usually requires additional security review; billing trigger created after Legal confirms effective date and Procurement confirms PO; possible split invoice for license + implementation services.

Mapping snippet (example YAML used by RevOps ingestion connector):
```yaml
contract_id: "C-2026-00345"
customer: "Acme Corp"
effective_date: "2026-01-05"
billing:
  model: "recurring"
  cadence: "monthly"
  start_date: "2026-02-01"
  currency: "USD"
  invoice_recipient: "finance@acme.example"
po:
  number: "PO-ACME-9876"
  received: true
rev_rec_flags:
  milestone_based: false
  prepaid: true
```

Operational exceptions & rules:
- If a PO is delayed >10 business days after contract effective date, RevOps may create an invoice and mark it as "PO_PENDING"; Procurement must escalate to sales and customer contacts to request PO or confirm payment terms.
- For amendments that change ARR by >10%, Sales must notify RevOps and FP&A immediately; RevOps will mark the contract as "amendment_pending" and FP&A will update forecast within 1 business day of confirmation.
- If Legal flags nonstandard rev-rec language (e.g., customer acceptance tied to variable success metrics), RevOps must not schedule billing automatically; Revenue recognition consultation with Accounting is required.

Dispute and remediation procedure:
1) Customer files billing dispute: Support tickets and Billing team triage within 2 business days.
2) If dispute caused by incorrect mapping (wrong PO, wrong start date), RevOps corrects the billing trigger and reissues invoice/credit within 5 business days.
3) If dispute is contractual, Legal and Sales coordinate a remediation amendment; RevOps holds impacted forecast movement until amendment final.

Operational checklists (quick reference):
- On contract signing: Sales uploads executed doc, tags RevOps, notifies Procurement if PO required.
- On RevOps intake: confirm currency, cadence, invoice recipient, and whether invoice should be prepaid or usage-settled.
- On PO mismatch: Procurement to record mismatch with reason code and escalate to Sales within 48 hours.

Metrics & reporting (what to monitor weekly):
- % of contracts with billing trigger created within SLA (target >= 95%).
- Average time (business days) from effective_date -> billing_trigger (target <= 3).
- Number of invoices with PO mismatch > 0 and days outstanding.
- Forecast delta due to amendments (weekly report to FP&A).

Implementation notes for integrations:
- RevOps connector must persist these fields in the invoice line: contract_id, po_number, original_effective_date, billing_cadence, rev_model. This enables deterministic linking for audits and RevRec reporting.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments we recommend tagging contract records with the deployment_region and hardware_commitment_id so that cost allocations can be reconciled to procurement spend.

Examples & sample timeline (typical Dedicated sale):
- Day 0: Contract signed (effective_date = Day 0).
- Day 1: Legal confirms effective date; Sales uploads to Salesforce.
- Day 2: Procurement confirms PO received and valid.
- Day 3: RevOps creates billing trigger; Billing system schedules first prepayment due Day 10.
- Day 4: FP&A updates forecast for the committed ARR.
